correctness.rationale: Minimal completeness/nonredundancy forces both exclusive-good classes to their sole approving agents; assigning t of c jointly approved goods to agent one yields utilities (a+t,b+c−t) of constant sum. Maximizing sorted Nash/leximin therefore minimizes |a−b−c+2t|. Binomial choices for t and a unique boundary optimum when |a−b|>c+1 give the exact formula including c=0; strict multiplicity occurs iff |a−b|<c. For random profiles C_m is binomial(m,p_m²), D_m is a centered bounded-increment sum with variance 2mp_m(1−p_m). Its stochastic scale sqrt(mp) meets mean shared count mp² exactly at mp³ order one. Subcritical proof handles bounded and diverging mp; supercritical Chebyshev; critical triangular-array CLT yields the erf law. Method-of-types entropy bounds for all c,t plus continuous mapping on |D|<C give the mixture distribution, with zero on the complementary event and continuous boundary entropy. Independently checked 330 (m,a,b,c) count triples including all c=0 and c=1 cases; the sample is finite corroboration of combinatorial formula, not of limiting CLT.

originality.rationale: Best-of-knowledge, not absolute priority: For two equally weighted labeled agents with iid Bernoulli approval of m labeled goods, count distinct cleaned optimal max-Nash/leximin allocations before deterministic tie-breaking. For exclusive counts a,b and common c, K=Σ_t binom(c,t)1{|a−b−c+2t|≤1}+1{|a−b|>c+1}, and K>1 iff |a−b|<c; the critical scale is p≈m^(−1/3), with limiting tie probability erf(λ^(3/2)/2) and an explicit mixture law for m^(−1/3)log K. value.rationale: Multiplicity before tie-breaking is mathematically meaningful for fair allocation correspondences: a deterministic rule conceals the number of optimal choices. The equality of jointly approved count mp² and random exclusive imbalance sqrt(mp) determines a natural cube-root sparsity threshold, a nontrivial error-function transition and a distributional entropy law of exponentially many labeled optimal allocations. This is more informative than mere existence of tied solutions and does not claim extension to many agents or correlated values.
